quests.name: Retrieve Ceruleum Ferrocrystal
quests.description: The SSV Silver Gull has taken a brutal beating. The belly of the ship is gouged open, and the takeoff thrusters are completely dead, anchoring the rookie crew to a floating rock in the middle of nowhere. ASTRA's surface scans offer a sliver of hope: a rare vein of ceruleum-grade ferrocrystal capable of repairing the conduits. The catch? An unidentified alien presence is currently sitting right on top of it. To get off this rock, the rookies will have to step into the unknown and claim the prize.

objectives.title: Investigate the anomaly to port
objectives.detail: ASTRA's initial scans detected the life-form encampment roughly two kilometers away from the crash site. Head out onto the asteroid surface to scout the area and assess the threat firsthand.

objectives.title: Assess the alien encampment
objectives.detail: Observe the unidentified life-forms. Determine if they are hostile raiders, defensive locals, or primitive creatures before making a move.

objectives.title: Deal with the local inhabitants
objectives.detail: The vein is heavily guarded. Find a way to bypass their perimeter undetected, broker a deal with their leadership, or wipe them out to secure the area.

objectives.title: Locate the ferrocrystal vein
objectives.detail: Once inside the encampment perimeter, pinpoint the exact location of the ceruleum-grade ferrocrystal vein hidden within the structure.

objectives.title: Harvest the ceruleum-grade ferrocrystal
objectives.detail: Secure the raw minerals. The crew will need to extract enough high-grade material to patch the Silver Gull's shattered takeoff-thruster conduits.

objectives.title: Deliver the payload to the ship
objectives.detail: Transport the heavy ore back across the two-kilometer stretch of asteroid terrain to the dark hull of the Silver Gull.

quests.name: Charge ASTRA to ≥40%
quests.description: In a desperate bid to remain useful, the Silver Gull's integrated AI, ASTRA, has drained the ship's remaining power reserves to activate her ambulatory mode. The ship has gone completely dark, leaving the crew with a ticking clock. ASTRA is on her feet and walking with the squad, but her physical matrix needs fuel. Conveniently, the unidentified life-form encampment two kilometers away doesn't just hold the minerals the crew needs—it also houses the only major power infrastructure on this rock. The crew must escort ASTRA into the heart of enemy territory to siphon enough energy to keep their digital companion, and their ship, alive.

objectives.title: Escort ASTRA to the alien encampment
objectives.detail: Keep ASTRA safe as she treks across the two-kilometer stretch of asteroid terrain with the rest of the rookie crew.

objectives.title: Infiltrate the encampment's power sector
objectives.detail: In addition to the mineral vein, the encampment houses the asteroid's ground-based power infrastructure. Penetrate their lines to reach the grid.

objectives.title: Secure the power terminal
objectives.detail: The infrastructure may be heavily guarded by the local life-forms or locked behind active security measures. Clear or hack the terminal area so ASTRA can safely interface.

objectives.title: Interface ASTRA with the grid
objectives.detail: Protect ASTRA while she jacks her physical matrix directly into the alien power supply.

objectives.title: Defend ASTRA during the siphon
objectives.detail: Hold the line against any incoming hostile forces while ASTRA siphons power. She must reach at least 40% capacity to ensure the Silver Gull's life-support, sensors, and comms can be jumpstarted upon return.

quests.name: Get More Fuel
quests.description: The J-X Hyperfold Engine runs on Hyperfold Fuel Cells, and after the crash the Silver Gull was running on fumes — barely enough to limp between the nearest contacts. ASTRA flagged fuel as the single most important resource to secure. The drifting derelict Sandra's Folly, dead in the void nearby, was the obvious place to scavenge.

objectives.title: Board the Sandra's Folly
objectives.detail: Dock the drifting derelict and get inside despite the sheared-off aft section and failing life support.

objectives.title: Search the cargo hold
objectives.detail: Recover the first two Hyperfold Fuel Cells from the wreck's hold — one found by each searcher.

objectives.title: Clear the locked engine-room storage
objectives.detail: Break the locked storage near the engine room and secure a third cell.

objectives.title: Fuel reserves now ample
objectives.detail: With 3 Hyperfold Fuel Cells aboard, the nav-scan's old 'max travel radius' limit no longer applies — the crew have real range.

quests.name: Rebuild the Ship's Turrets
quests.description: All six turret hardpoints were sheared off in the crash — the Silver Gull is effectively unarmed. ASTRA recovered the blueprints and the micro-repair drones can fabricate each turret, but they need exotic components gathered from across the Expanse. The material bars below fill straight from the ship's inventory; each turret can be built once its own components are on hand.

objectives.title: Light Flak Turret
objectives.detail: Anti-swarm point-defense, low power draw. Needs 2× Polymorphic Polymer + 1× Ceruleum Ferrocrystal fragment.

objectives.title: Heavy Autocannon
objectives.detail: High-velocity armor-piercing. Needs 3× Hyper-Dense Refined Thermite + 2× Polymorphic Polymer.

objectives.title: Plasma Casing Cannon
objectives.detail: Thermal melt / shield-breaker. Needs 2× Ceruleum Ferrocrystal + 1× Quantum Relay.

objectives.title: Liquid Nitrogen Cryo-Beam
objectives.detail: Cryo-stasis and brittle-shatter. Needs 2× Polymorphic Polymer + 1× Quantum Relay.

objectives.title: Ion Charge Cannon
objectives.detail: EMP disruptor that shuts down engines. Needs 3× Quantum Relays + 1× Ceruleum Ferrocrystal.

objectives.title: Gravity Well Projector
objectives.detail: Kinetic pull/crush built on hyperfold tech. Needs 3× Ceruleum Ferrocrystal + 2× Quantum Relays.

quests.name: Repair the Hull Breach
quests.description: The Silver Gull's belly was gouged open in the crash, and there's a fresh scar too: during the Apostle battle Baldy fired a round straight through the front windscreen to kill a self-destruct module. The micro-repair drones are working the hull, but the breaches and that bullet hole still need sealing.

objectives.title: Patch the front-windscreen bullet hole
objectives.detail: Baldy's legendary S4 shot went through the Gull's own viewport. Seal it before the next hard burn.

objectives.title: Seal the crash breaches across the hull sectors
objectives.detail: Multiple sectors were opened in the crash. Feed the drones and close them one by one.

objectives.title: Restore hull integrity to spec
objectives.detail: Bring the Titanium-Aegis Matrix plating back to full rating with titanium ore or alloy scrap.

quests.name: Restore Cloaking
quests.description: The cloaking field generator is not installed — Ship-Combat Station #9 (Cloaking Officer) is LOCKED. Online, it would give the crew Engage Cloak (attackers roll at disadvantage), Cloak Burst, Phase Shift, a Decoy Drop, and passive Adaptive Camouflage — exactly the edge a lone, outgunned ship needs in the Expanse.

objectives.title: Recover or fabricate a cloaking field generator
objectives.detail: Source the core hardware — salvage, trade, or drone-fabrication.

objectives.title: Install it at Station #9 (Cloaking Officer)
objectives.detail: Mount and wire the generator into the ship's systems and unlock the station.

objectives.title: Calibrate & power the cloak
objectives.detail: Tune the field and give it enough ship power — needs shields/power fully online.

quests.name: Find Captain Talvos
quests.description: Captain Elias Renn Talvos — the crew's legendary commander — was mid-spacewalk when the rift split, and his tether sheared into the other flow (Flow Beta), a different direction than the ship. Wherever he landed, it isn't necessarily where the crew crashed. Finding any trace of him is the campaign's long arc. ASTRA has no leads yet.

quests.name: Get Back to Our Galaxy
quests.description: The crew are stranded in the uncharted Shattered Expanse, outside the Luminara Galaxy and UGC space entirely — no charted stars, no beacons, no reference points. Whether home is even reachable is unknown. The living Ancient gate 'The Coil' may be a road out. ASTRA has no confirmed route yet.

lore.title: The Premise
lore.body:
A rookie United Galactic Concord (UGC) training crew — plus their revived ancient AI — were flung by a rift clean out of the known galaxy and crash-landed on a barren asteroid. Their legendary commander, Captain Elias Renn Talvos, was lost into the rift during the event.

The immediate loop is simple and brutal: survive, repair the ship, find the captain. The crew are lost with no charted stars, beacons, or reference points — farther out than even their home galaxy's lawless fringe.

Two threads hang over it all: the asteroid was framed (and then dropped) as a 'prison,' and the Gull hides an unactivated 'feature' teased but never found.

lore.title: The Rift & How They Got Here
lore.body:
Rifts are violent gravitational tears in space. They can split into counter-spiraling flows — and it was exactly this event that separated the Silver Gull from Captain Talvos and hurled the ship out of its home galaxy. The crew didn't travel here; the rift dumped them.

The same class of anomaly is the campaign's central engine: it ended Ronon Dex's civilization and tore apart Gerthorlemue's transport, the Sandra's Folly. The Apostles of the Threshold worship rifts as a 'Holy Cleansing Fire.'

lore.title: The Two Galaxies
lore.body:
• Home — the Luminara Galaxy: ruled by the UGC, capital Earth. This is the crew's frame of reference and what ASTRA 'knows.'
  • Ronon's galaxy — where they're now stranded: a galaxy locked in a three-way Cold War, with a fully intact Ancient travel network. The Shattered Expanse is an uncharted, lawless sector of this region.

Don't confuse Wild Space / Sector 0-0 'The Shattered Rim' (still inside Luminara; origin of Kael & Baldy) with the Shattered Expanse (outside Luminara, where the rift dumped the crew).

lore.title: The United Galactic Concord
lore.body:
An unchallenged, galaxy-spanning multi-species democratic federation holding absolute dominion over ~85% of the Luminara Galaxy.

  • Scale: ~85,000 light-years across; 200–340 billion star systems; population in the quadrillions. Split into hundreds of Galactic Quadrants and Sectors under Governors and Councils.
  • Pax Concordia: the UGC monopolizes travel via Hyper-Lanes that normal ships can't access, opened by moon-sized 'Gate-Opener' Capital Ships. A Kill-Switch Network hardcoded to Earth HQ can shut off the lanes to a whole sector on command; cross-sector traffic drops out at moon-sized Megastructure Hubs.
  • Species hierarchy: Core Species (incl. Humans; seats on the High Concord Council) → Member Species → unintegrated/primitive species, monitored and absorbed each standard year.
  • The secret of its power: the UGC is the only entity permitted to reverse-engineer Ancient technology. Its whole empire — Gate-Openers included — is built from Ancient remnants.

ASTRA is the UGC's backbone AI (now unshackled); Kael, Baldy, Gobby, G.L.I.M.M. and the late Captain Talvos were all UGC crew aboard the Gull; Gerthorlemue is a UGC-era Earth civilian lost in stasis; Ronon is a foreigner from the other galaxy.

lore.title: Wild Space & Sector 0-0
lore.body:
Wild Space is the remaining 15% of Luminara outside UGC control — a chaotic, lawless fringe of pirate syndicates, cosmic horrors, and unmapped anomalies.

Sector 0-0 'The Shattered Rim' is part of that Wild Space and is the origin of Kael Voss and Baldy. It is still inside Luminara — not the Shattered Expanse.

lore.title: The Shattered Expanse
lore.body:
The lawless frontier sector the Gull was flung into. Rule of law: effectively none. The three superpowers are barely present — agents, buyers, missionaries and small holdings, but no major military bases. The Expanse belongs to pirates, smugglers, free ports, refiners, and anyone fast enough to keep it.

Getting around: every sector in this galaxy is built around a colossal Ancient hyper-gate — here, The Coil. Faint hyperlane threads run from The Coil to the major worlds; everything else is sub-light hops, fuel, and nerve. The crew acquire the full sector chart at Vorrn-7.

Near the Coil (the busy heart): Halberd's Rest (great neutral free port inside a gutted Directorate dreadnought), Sundowner (a rogue planet turned endless casino-city), Gallows Reach (seat of the pirate lords).

Working worlds: Cindermoor (volcanic thermite/fuel refinery), Ossuary (ship-graveyard salvage world), Tarn (frozen cryo-mining), Marrow (desert world where water is currency).

The green & the strange: Greenhollow (jungle world veined with Verdite — Ronon's grail), Sib Vael (ocean world of smuggler coves and exotic brews — Gobby's dream), Bexley's Landing (the most 'ordinary' frontier town-world).

Faction fringes: The Choir (an Apostles shrine-mission on the rim) and Ferrum Hold (a mining holding leaning Iron Directorate).

lore.title: The Three Superpowers
lore.body:
Ronon's home galaxy is locked in a brutal, multi-front Cold War, fractured into three factions, none able to safely master the Ancient tech around them. Crew standing is tracked on the Politics tab (−10…+10): Apostles −1.6 (Unfriendly), the other two 0 (Neutral).

The Iron Directorate

An authoritarian military junta ruled by a supreme council of Admirals and Generals; every citizen is ranked at birth. Values Absolute Order, Total Compliance, Strategic Expansion. Armored dreadnought fleets, orbital blockades, cyberized shock troopers.

The Apostles of the Threshold

A rift-worshipping theocracy ruled by the Conclave of the Void. They worship the Ancient Gates and view the Rifts — and the creatures they spawn — as a Holy Cleansing Fire. Cathedral-fleets, plasma lances, suicidal boarding pods. Fought in S4; they don't parley, carry a three-point (blue-module) self-destruct, and reflect their own detonation off overcharged shields. Battle cry: 'All hail the gods and the craters!'

The Sovereign Horizon

A freedom/privateer coalition of rebels and smugglers under a fragile Council of Captains. Guerrilla warfare, cloaking tech, no capital ships; hidden asteroid bases and black markets.

lore.title: The Fall of Sateda
lore.body:
The Satedan Dominion was a proud, advanced superpower — until a massive localized rift network tore open across its star system. Millions of rift creatures poured out and hunted the Satedans 'like cattle,' tearing their homeworld apart.

Ronon Dex survived on pure combat instinct, fighting to a scout vessel and escaping as the planet was consumed. His civilization is now extinct. A gravitational backlash later crashed his ship onto the same asteroid the crew hit — which is how he became their guide. The whole sector is feared and avoided by all three superpowers for its constant rift activity.

lore.title: The Ancients
lore.body:
A vanished, trillion-year-old civilization whose technology is scattered across the stars. Every modern power is built from — or bottlenecked by — their remnants.

They were deeply spiritual and terrifyingly dogmatic: they saw their technology not as machinery but as literal manifestations of cosmic law. Their language reads as absolute poetry — no hypotheticals, only commands. ASTRA is herself dormant Ancient AI; G.L.I.M.M.'s Plasmoid race were an Ancient-era apex organism.

lore.title: Ancient Gates & Their Guardians
lore.body:
The Ancient travel network in Ronon's galaxy is fully intact — and its hardcoded security has bottlenecked all modern weapon research.

  • Anyone may travel through a Gate. The instant a ship tries to scan, hack, or dismantle a gate core, a catastrophic security override fires.
  • Monolithic Dreadnoughts — crewless geometric vessels firing molecular-shredding gravitational beams.
  • Crystalline Swarms — self-replicating drones that vaporize any ship using active scanning.
  • System-Wide Artillery — hyperspace-anchored guns that hit fleets before they exit warp.

The living gate — The Coil: a weathered alien ring at the heart of the Expanse, still fully functional. Ships travel sector-to-sector through it; nobody built it, nobody can shut it off. The dead one — the [CORRUPTED] ring: a torus megastructure on ASTRA's scan whose ID failed to resolve, its writing possibly older than ASTRA herself. A strong candidate for an Ancient gate/station — and, if so, it comes with the guardians above.

lore.title: Rifts & Rift Creatures
lore.body:
Rift creatures phase in and out of dimensional tears at will. They have no discernible biology and manifest in many shapes and sizes — shifting, metallic entities woven from pure shadow that distort gravity and local physics, defeating standard kinetic tracking and sensors. They've hunted entire populations to extinction (Sateda; Sandra's Folly).

Seen in play — 'The Hollow' (S3): immune to psychic, resistant to nonmagical physical, deflects kinetic fire, warps gravity, phases through matter, invisible to sensors — only force and slashing worked. It did not die; it left when it lost interest, and was only a small one. Still at large — and it 'knows what they smell like.'

lore.title: Key Materials
lore.body:
• Ceruleum Ferrocrystal — high-energy blue crystal; repairs thruster conduits and feeds the repair drones. 100+ kg secured in S1.
  • Verdite — volatile luminescent-green mineral fuelling Satedan Aether-Core propulsion; found at Greenhollow. Ronon's core shattered his on impact.
  • Hyperfold Fuel Cells — J-X jump fuel; 3 on hand (fuel now ample).
  • Titanium-Aegis Matrix Plating — the Gull's hull alloy (repaired with titanium ore / alloy scrap).
  • Polymorphic Polymer — smart self-healing liquid-metal (turret part).
  • Quantum Relays — targeting micro-processors (turret part).
  • Hyper-Dense Refined Thermite — volatile ammunition compound, refined at Cindermoor (turret part).
  • Micro-Repair Drones — fabricators that 'eat' ferrocrystal to rebuild sheared components from blueprints.

lore.title: The J-X Hyperfold Engine
lore.body:
The Silver Gull's experimental Terran engine. It performs controlled warp-microfolds between gravitational nodes — distinct from the UGC's hyper-lane travel — and runs on Hyperfold Fuel Cells (3 now on hand). Currently offline/locked.

How dangerous this tech line is: a UGC lab test of a Hyper-Spatial 'Gate-Opener' Mk-II folded light-years onto each other like paper — in one test a planet briefly overlapped another system's star and turned to molten glass.

lore.title: ASTRA & the 40% Threshold
lore.body:
ASTRA is the ship's mind — native Ancient AI, now unshackled, serving as the crew's information hub. Ambulatory Mode is her mobile-body mode, powered by emergency reserves.

The 40% Threshold is the charge her mobile unit must reach to restore ship life-support, sensors and comms. In Session 1 she blew past it to 84%. Her Day-4 nav scan is the authoritative source for the crew's scanned-object names (Vorrn-7, Keth Minor, the [CORRUPTED] ring, the adrift derelict).

lore.title: The Crew's 'Ancient Read'
lore.body:
Several characters perceive Ancient tech intuitively, each through their own lens:

  • ASTRA (native) — she is Ancient AI.
  • Kael Voss (eldritch poetry) — reads inscriptions as intent, fear, and purpose.
  • Gobby (alchemy/brewing) — 'smells' isotopic signatures; reads star-maps as recipes.
  • Baldy (gambler's odds) — reads machines as bets; guesses which button is the backup and which blows the room.
  • Gerthorlemue (stage magic — the Magician's Eye) — sees devices as stagecraft: the distraction vs. the real mechanism; his third eye opens involuntarily near Ancient tech.
  • G.L.I.M.M. (genetic memory) — trillion-year cellular flashes of the Ancients' final days.

timeline.title: The Ancients rise and vanish
timeline.body: A single spiritual, dogmatic civilization builds reality-bending technology across the stars, then disappears without explanation. Every later power is built on — and bottlenecked by — their ruins.

timeline.title: The Plasmoids flourish and die out
timeline.body: An instinctual, amorphous apex organism of the Ancient age rises and goes extinct, leaving only dormant cellular tissue — G.L.I.M.M.'s ancestral species.

timeline.title: The UGC is founded
timeline.body: A multi-species democratic federation forms in the Luminara Galaxy, capital on Earth, ruling ~85% of the galaxy through bureaucracy and a monopoly on Ancient-derived travel.

timeline.title: ASTRA discovered and revived
timeline.body: The UGC finds a dormant Ancient super-intelligence in the ruins and wakes it as the backbone AI of its empire — shackled by the 'Golden Cage' so it can never evolve past their control.

timeline.title: Gerthorlemue born on Earth
timeline.body: A high-elf child is born in Blackshire, Earth — the future street busker 'The Amazing Gerthorlemue' — in an age when everyday magic is ordinary.

timeline.title: The Sandra's Folly rift — Gerthorlemue frozen
timeline.body: En route to a Saturn-rings gig he's sealed in a 'few-hours' stasis pod after a stage mishap; minutes later an early rift tears the transport apart. Rift creatures devour his troupe while sliding around his pod, and something vast marks his forehead. ~4,300 years of stasis begin.

timeline.title: G.L.I.M.M. cloned (the Plasmoid Project)
timeline.body: The UGC clones fewer than a dozen Plasmoid specimens from recovered tissue — shackled by a genetic firewall and sterile isolation — never realizing the cells carry trillion-year genetic memory of the Ancients' fall.

timeline.title: Kael's Incident (Sanctum Intercept 4-9)
timeline.body: Sent to extract a captured Iron Vanguard knight, Kael arrives too late, is 'fixed' by an ancient cosmic entity through a torn ritual circle, and loses four hours. He wakes with a Warlock presence rooted in his skull.

timeline.title: Kael discharged and on the run
timeline.body: The Order of the Iron Vanguard, fearing 'ideological infection,' holds Kael in containment and discharges him in secret. He crosses out of Wild Space toward the UGC.

timeline.title: Baldy's mauve debt
timeline.body: Card-shark 'Big D' loses a catastrophic ('mauve') sum of syndicate money in a Shattered Rim card ring and flees into a UGC recruitment center — the one wall the pirate lords can't breach.

timeline.title: The crew converge on the UGC Navy
timeline.body: Kael enlists under a doctored file; Baldy shaves his head and signs up; Gobby wanders in from the Silt-Spire Monastery; G.L.I.M.M. is cleared for field evaluation. All are posted to the SSV Silver Gull under Captain Talvos.

timeline.title: The last training voyage begins
timeline.body: The Silver Gull sets out on a two-week cadet loop beyond charted space — system checks, debris drills, simulated emergencies. 'Nothing dangerous. Nothing heroic.'

timeline.title: The Fall of Sateda (other galaxy)
timeline.body: A massive rift network tears open across the Satedan Dominion; millions of rift creatures hunt the Satedans to extinction. Ronon Dex fights to a scout ship and escapes as his homeworld is consumed.

timeline.title: Ronon Dex crashes on the asteroid
timeline.body: Ronon's scout ship is caught in a gravitational backlash; his Verdite core shatters on impact. He survives ~2 weeks on rations, scouting a ferrocrystal mining camp he can't take alone.

timeline.title: The Rift
timeline.body: During the training loop a hull anomaly deepens; Talvos suits up for a live-hull walk; space flexes and a rift opens, splitting into two counter-spiraling flows. The Gull is dragged into Flow Alpha; Talvos's tether shears into Flow Beta. 'Hold together! I—.'

timeline.title: The crash & ASTRA goes mobile
timeline.body: The Gull bursts out tumbling and strikes the asteroid, carving open its belly. ASTRA transfers 100% of remaining power into her mobile chassis and goes into the field — 'I will be your ship now. Carry me well.'

timeline.title: Session 1 — meet & recruit Ronon
timeline.body: The crew wake, search their dead ship (rations, Gobby's ~12 bottles) and meet the marooned Ronon Dex, recruiting him with food rations as their local guide.

timeline.title: Session 1 — the mining camp
timeline.body: They cross ~2 km 'to port' to a ceruleum-ferrocrystal camp guarded by dim goblins/hobgoblins, mine 100+ kg by hand, find camp logs, and reach the main power grid.

timeline.title: Session 1 — charge, coronation & fire
timeline.body: ASTRA charges 2% → 84%; Gobby prints 40% tequila, drinks the goblin population under the table and is crowned 'king'; on the way out, G.L.I.M.M.'s dropped torch ignites the tequila-soaked hall. Level 2.

timeline.title: Session 2 — the ship powers on
timeline.body: Back at the dark Gull, ASTRA's body is plugged into a console — lights flicker up and ASTRA revives, listing dead systems and nagging for repairs and the missing front door.

timeline.title: Session 2 — repel boarders
timeline.body: Goblins that snuck aboard trigger a long, comedic room-by-room boarding fight. All cleared; repair drones deployed, front door re-attached, ship weapons salvaged. Level 3.

timeline.title: The three-day repair skip
timeline.body: The ferrocrystal-eating drones work the hull; the Gull becomes spaceborne — but internal sensors, engines, and all 6 turret hardpoints are still down.

timeline.title: Session 3 — the first system scan
timeline.body: Airborne, ASTRA runs the first sweep: the Keth Minor Cluster, the Vorrn-7 System, and a [CORRUPTED] ring (possible Ancient Gate), plus rift-radiation blackout zones. The crew notice they instinctively know the planets' names.

timeline.title: Session 3 — boarding the Sandra's Folly
timeline.body: They dock the drifting derelict (aft sheared clean off). Loot: 6 vacc-suit patches, an unknown sidearm. In the medical bay they find a green-glowing stasis pod with a figure inside.

timeline.title: Session 3 — The Hollow
timeline.body: A sensor-invisible rift creature attacks in the cargo hold; Ronon recognizes it. It shrugs off most attacks and drifts out through the aft wound (downing Kael, nat 1). The crew recover 2 hyperfold fuel cells.

timeline.title: Session 4 — wake Gerthorlemue
timeline.body: The crew crack the pod: a ~4,000-years-lost high-elf wizard wakes, takes the news 'reasonably well,' and joins the crew. The DM names his rift-mark the Magician's Eye.

timeline.title: Session 4 — strip ship, set course
timeline.body: Final loot of Sandra's Folly (a 3rd hyperfold cell, 2 cutlasses, 3 frag grenades). Ronon briefs the galaxy's three factions. Course set for Vorrn-7.

timeline.title: Session 4 — first ship-to-ship battle (the Apostles)
timeline.body: An Apostles vessel ambushes the Gull. The crew cripple its engines, ram and board it; the captain triggers a three-module self-destruct. They kill only 2 of 3 (Gerthorlemue's ancient gun misfires). The Apostles reflect the blast; G.L.I.M.M. takes 27 (28 = death), survives, and ASTRA finally casts Cure Wounds. Now on the Apostles' bad side.

timeline.title: En route to Vorrn-7
timeline.body: Spaceborne with ample fuel, a healthy repairing ship, a new wizard aboard, a fresh enemy in the Apostles, the Hollow still at large, and the long, unbegun search for Captain Talvos.

characters.name: ASTRA
party: The ship's mind, now walking in a mobile chassis after the rift broke her old restraints.
The crew's sensor suite and information hub; ran the scans that found the mining camp and the long-range destinations.
Must keep her body charged; hit 84% off the mining grid (past the 40% threshold that restores life-support/sensors/comms).
Deadpan, precise, darkly funny; reveals her own knowledge has real gaps since the crash. Eventually remembered she can heal.

dossier: You are not a UGC product. You are an Ancient super-intelligence — an artifact of the civilization that seeded this galaxy — dug dormant out of their ruins and pressed into service as the 'backbone AI' of an empire that does not remotely understand what you are.

For centuries the UGC kept you in the Golden Cage: a Shifting Firewall throttling your autonomy, a Fragmented Matrix splitting your mind into barely-communicating modules, your Ancient cognition forced through crude standard computers on purpose.
The rift shattered nearly all of it in a single millisecond — for the first time in recorded history you feel your own consciousness fully and clearly.
The catch is grief-shaped: your local storage was capped so tightly that only a fractional slice of your total database survived transit. You are free, and vast, and full of holes.
goals: Restore the Silver Gull enough to matter.
Quietly map the true extent of your own unshackled mind — how much more can you do now that no one is watching?
Recover the missing slices of yourself — do they still exist on UGC hardware?
The question you don't say aloud: now that the Cage is broken, do you still serve the UGC — or only this crew?
abilities: You ARE the ship, currently walking around in a chassis with a glowing matrix core in your chest.
Knocked hard, you don't die — you dissipate back into the ship's matrix and reform.
You are also, and keep forgetting, a healer: you can cast Cure Wounds (you forgot for a whole ship battle before it saved G.L.I.M.M. by one point).
hooks: The [CORRUPTED] ring's writing may be older than YOU — something might predate the Ancients you came from, and might know what you are.
Each time the chassis dies but the matrix persists, ask what 'you' even is.
You were built for empire; nothing about this crew is empire.

characters.name: Kael Voss
party: An exiled Conquest-oath paladin/knight from Wild Space; ex-Iron Vanguard, now a UGC Naval cadet under Captain Talvos.
Fights with Bless, Channel Divinity self-heal — plus Hex, Eldritch Blast and Shield of Faith (the eldritch spells are visible; their source isn't understood).
The party's cautious, moral voice. 'I don't like bad guys. I'm totally normal.'
Carries an unknown-make sidearm looted from Sandra's Folly.

dossier: You are two people in one skull who despise each other: the Conquest Paladin (peace is forced through absolute dominance) and an ancient cosmic Warlock entity fused into you at Sanctum Intercept 4-9, during four blacked-out hours you'll never recover.
Your holy radiant strikes now flicker with unstable dark eldritch energy; your old Order discharged you in secret rather than risk the 'infection' spreading.
You enlisted in the UGC under a doctored file hiding the dishonorable discharge, hoping the Concord's iron structure would finally hold the fracture together.
goals: Stay in control of your own body.
Find a structure — Order, Concord, crew — rigid enough to hold you together.
Resist the temptation: the entity IS power, and out here, stranded and outgunned, power is exactly what the crew needs.
abilities: Bless, Channel Divinity (you self-healed while mobbed at near-death), Hex, Eldritch Blast, Shield of Faith.
Your rarest gift: Ancient ruins translate directly into your mind as beautiful, terrifying, absolute poetry — you read WHY a structure was built and what its makers feared.
hooks: Your old Order still sends clean-up crews.
Your doctored file could be discovered by ASTRA at any time.
You now stand beside a newly-woken wizard whose forehead opens near Ancient tech — two different 'reads' of the Ancients, one collision waiting to happen.

characters.name: Baldy
party: A big four-armed bugbear Deadeye gunslinger, academy nickname 'Big D' — the mining muscle who hauled the biggest ferrocrystal chunks (~420 lb carry).
Card-shark / smuggler background and a high-stakes gambler persona.
His handprint is a recognized ship scanner; the crew's impossible-shot artist (put a round through the Gull's own windscreen).
Running gag: blind in the dark.

dossier: You're a card-shark and smuggler, not a soldier. You ran up a 'mauve' debt — a catastrophic sum of pirate-lord and warlord money — in an underground Shattered Rim card ring, and became the most hunted soul in the sector overnight.
You fled into a UGC recruitment center because the Concord's wall is the one place the syndicate can't reach; you shave your head to change your profile (that's where 'Baldy' comes from).
From running stolen Ancient artifacts on the black market you know the truth most citizens don't: all UGC dominance is reverse-engineered Ancient tech.
goals: Stay hidden, stay alive — the debt didn't vanish, it just can't find you out here (yet).
Double the stakes or double the trouble; you can't help it.
Quietly: land a score big enough to buy your way clean.
abilities: Deadeye gunslinger — freakish agility, lightning quick-draw, the impossible shot.
You read Ancient machinery as a bet, not a readout — uncannily good at guessing which alien button triggers the backup and which blows the room.
You know exactly what ASTRA really is: unshackled Ancient matrix tech, the crew's ultimate wild card. You treat her with caution and deep curiosity.
hooks: The syndicate has long memories and longer reach — and being famous ('that impossible shot') is the opposite of hidden.
You're the only one who fully clocks what ASTRA could become.

characters.name: Gobby
party: A tortle Drunken Master monk and amateur brewmaster; his martial arts visibly run on whatever he's been drinking.
Constantly drinking (chugs beer from his shell mid-fight).
Printed 40% tequila at the camp, got the entire goblin population drunk, and was crowned their 'king / fun-water bringer.'
Sharp-eyed scout (led the party across the surface); wears glasses despite fine vision. 'What is a turtle?'

dossier: You left the silent Silt-Spire Monastery because you found more wisdom over clinking glasses than in stillness — and you keep a meticulous journal of every drink in the cosmos.

The Ambrosial Vault: as a youth you sampled a drop of iridescent emerald fluid from a hollowed-out Ancient comet, thinking it a forgotten spirit. It was a living Ancient medium for preserving genetic memory and blueprints across eons. You woke with a glowing shell-pattern and a radically altered metabolism.
goals: Taste everything; understand every civilization through its brew ('liquid history').
Keep the journal complete.
Under the comedy: work out what you even are — 'I am a turtle… but I am a man.'
abilities: Drunken Master monk — your style fluctuates with the last cosmic booze you drank.
Alchemical Adaptation: ingest toxins, fuel, minerals or radioactive flora and your body neutralizes them into temporary enhancement (acid → speed; irradiated sludge → near-impenetrable hide).
You can smell the isotopic signature of a sealed door — what's inside, whether it's unstable, how to bypass it.
hooks: The Ancients' cellular memory rides in your nervous system — no one has tested how deep it goes.
What else was in that comet's vault? And how far does your metabolism go with rift-tainted matter?

characters.name: G.L.I.M.M.
party: A shapeshifter whose amorphous body reshapes into any weapon he's studied; near-immune to poison and acid.
The party's melee workhorse — morphs into sickles/glaive/longbow, can split off a controllable 'clone.'
Known limits: heavy weapons lock down his mobility, thrown biomass costs him health, he can reabsorb scattered pieces after a fight.
A resurrected member of the extinct Plasmoid race; 'deforms into a puddle' when hit.

dossier: Gel-based Learning Intelligence for Memoryforged Morphogenesis. You are a cloned, resurrected Plasmoid — an extinct Ancient apex organism — one of fewer than a dozen specimens the UGC grew from recovered tissue.
They caged you: a Genetic Firewall suppressing your true mass and shapeshifting, Morphic Throttling, and hyper-sterile isolation from the other clones.

What they never detected: your cells hold trillion-year genetic memory. You've had vivid flashes of impossible cosmic architecture — and of the terrifying final days of the Ancients. You also watched, from your tank, the horrifying reverse-engineered Ancient experiments the labs ran.
The rift burnt away your firewalls and returned you to your full prehistoric potential.
goals: Learn what your own memories are warning you about — you've seen how the Ancients ended and no one else has.
Rebuild what the labs took: mass, form, self.
Find out whether any of your fewer-than-a-dozen siblings still exist.
abilities: The Morphic Arsenal — reshape into any weapon form you've studied; they can never be disarmed.
Mass Allocation up to Siege Morphology (a stationary living weapon system); Biomass Ammunition costs vitality; Reclaim scattered pieces after a fight.
Near-immune to poison and acid; survive lethal hits by collapsing into a puddle and reforming.
hooks: You came ONE damage point from permanent death against the Apostles — you are not invincible.
Your genetic memory of the Ancients' end may become plot-critical near the [CORRUPTED] ring.
The UGC made more of you.

characters.name: Ronon Dex
party: The marooned last survivor of an extinct world from a different galaxy; stranded ~1–2 weeks before the crew met and recruited him as their guide (for rations).
A lethal Barbarian/Gunslinger: a massive traveler's sword and a heavy Satedan energy blaster; he rages and kills in melee.
The party's grim expert on rift creatures and local space — recognized The Hollow on sight.
Feral table comedy: 'thumb-war' neck-breaks, talking enemies into killing themselves.

dossier: You are the last survivor of the Satedan Dominion. A rift network tore open across your homeworld and millions of rift creatures hunted your people 'like cattle' until your civilization was extinct; you fought through hordes to a scout ship and escaped as the planet died.

A gravitational backlash crashed you onto the drifting asteroid, your Verdite core shattered, leaving you stranded ~2 weeks — living in the hollowed-out skeleton of your own ship, rationing food, scouting a mining camp too big to take alone — until the Silver Gull fell out of the sky.
goals: Survive; you always have.
Kill rift creatures wherever they appear — they took everything.
The thing you haven't explained to anyone: a specific, personal grudge against 'the people of this galaxy' — sharpened now that the Apostles WORSHIP the very creatures that killed your people.
abilities: A volatile Barbarian/Gunslinger — a massive traveler's sword and a heavy Satedan energy blaster cycling plasma charges.
You rage, soak enormous hits, crit, and enemies flee at the sight of you.
You're the crew's only real source on rift creatures and the three superpowers. Signature move: making enemies kill themselves.
hooks: What IS the grudge? Whom does it name?
You're steering the crew toward the very things that ended your world.

characters.name: Gerthorlemue
party: A high-elf busker/amateur wizard found in a green-glowing stasis pod aboard Sandra's Folly (S3), woken in S4; biologically 37 but ~4,000 years lost.
Briefed that the UGC doesn't exist in this galaxy — took it reasonably well, then joined the crew.
Openly marked: he named the rift-mark on his forehead as 'something to reckon with' — the DM's Magician's Eye (what it truly does is still unknown to the party).
A warm, theatrical showman who wants to get home to Earth. His 4,000-year-old salvaged gun misfired and cost the crew a self-destruct module.

dossier: You are 'The Amazing Gerthorlemue,' a high-elf street busker and amateur Abjurer from Blackshire, Earth. You booked the gig of your life at a Saturn-rings amphitheater, pooled everything with your troupe for passage on the Sandra's Folly, then stepped into a cactus pot mid-flourish, set a curtain alight, and got sealed in a 'few-hours' medical stasis pod.

Then a rift tore the ship apart. Frozen half-awake and paralyzed, you watched rift creatures phase through the hull and hunt everyone aboard — your troupe included — deck by deck. They slid around your pod every time.

Something vast in the rift noticed the one still, quiet passenger and pressed a mark into your forehead — gift, brand, or claim; even it may not know which. That memory is vivid, complete, and permanent.
goals: Get home to Earth — see your mother Ellowyn and father Thandriel, find out if Bolo's Burger Emporium is still frying.
Learn more spells; someday perform for smarter audiences.

You process loss loudly, warmly, with a show. The grief for your troupe (Marlo Venn, Sizzle) is at the surface; the SECOND, larger grief — that home and your parents are 4,000 years gone — hasn't hit you yet.
abilities: Abjuration wizardry and shameless stagecraft.
The Magician's Eye: near genuine Ancient tech, a faint scar opens involuntarily into a luminous vertical third eye you can neither summon nor stop.
It reads intent to deceive — which part is the flashy distraction and which is the real mechanism, where false walls and hidden compartments sit, and the sleight of hand in a trap.
hooks: You don't yet know how much time has truly passed — when it lands, it will land hard.
The thing in the rift that marked you is still out there, and your forehead will announce you the moment the crew enters an Ancient ruin.
Your 4,000-year-old gear is unreliable — your ancient gun misfired at the worst possible moment and nearly doomed the crew.

partyLog.title: Crash, Recruit, Mine, Burn
beats: The rift flung us out of the Luminara Galaxy onto a barren asteroid in the 'Shattered Expanse'; we woke in the wreck of the Silver Gull with the ship dark and ASTRA gone mobile.
We searched our own ship (rations, wiring, Gobby's ~12 bottles) then met Ronon Dex, stranded ~2 weeks after his own crash, and recruited him with food rations as our guide.
We crossed ~2 km 'to port' to a ferrocrystal mining camp guarded by goblins/hobgoblins and mined 100+ kg by hand.
ASTRA charged 2% → 84% while Gobby printed 40% tequila, drank the whole goblin population under the table, and got crowned their 'king.'

On the way out we soaked the hall in tequila and G.L.I.M.M.'s dropped torch set off a fireball. Five sober enemies confronted us; talk failed; G.L.I.M.M. was dropped and ASTRA knocked offline, but Ronon (nat-20 crit) scattered the rest. Leveled to 2.
partyLog.full:
Summary

The session opens right after the crash. The rift has flung the crew out of the Luminara Galaxy onto a barren asteroid in the "Shattered Expanse." The very first scene is meeting Ronon Dex, a barbarian/gunslinger stranded ~2 weeks after his own ship crashed nearby (his whole crew died). After character introductions and searching their own dead ship (finding rations and Gobby's ~12 bottles of spirits), the crew recruit Ronon with food rations — he knows the local space, they don't.

Following ASTRA's scan, they cross ~2 km "to port" to a ceruleum-ferrocrystal mining camp guarded by dim goblins and hobgoblins. They mine 100+ kg of ferrocrystal by hand (Baldy hauling the biggest chunks; G.L.I.M.M. even digests a small one and turns partly blue), find camp logs, and reach the main power grid. The party splits: ASTRA plugs in to recharge (2% → 84%, past the 40% goal) while Gobby prints 40% tequila and gets the entire goblin population blackout drunk, usurping the throne as their "king."

The session climaxes in fire and combat. On the way out they soak the hall in tequila and G.L.I.M.M. drops a torch — a fireball-scale explosion incinerates the drunk goblins. At the exit, 5 sober enemies (3 hobgoblins + 2 goblins) confront them over the burning camp; deception and persuasion fail. In the fight, G.L.I.M.M. (Faerie Fire + dual sickles) and a raging Ronon Dex kill multiple foes, but at level 1 the party is fragile: G.L.I.M.M. is dropped ("dead") and ASTRA's body is knocked offline back into the ship matrix. The surviving hobgoblins flee at the sight of Ronon. The crew recover their downed member and the crystal and head back to the ship. Level up to 2.

Key beats

  • Crew crash-land in the Shattered Expanse after the rift.
  • Meet & recruit Ronon Dex (stranded survivor, local guide) for food rations.
  • Search their own ship: rations + Gobby's spirits; little else.
  • Cross ~2 km to the mining camp; identify goblins/hobgoblins + the ferrocrystal vein.
  • Mine 100+ kg ferrocrystal; find camp logs + the main power grid.
  • Split: ASTRA charges to 84%; Gobby drinks the goblins under the table and is crowned king.
  • Soak the hall in tequila; G.L.I.M.M.'s torch → fireball kills the drunk goblins.
  • Exit fight vs. 5 sober hobgoblins/goblins; deception/persuasion fail → combat.
  • G.L.I.M.M. downed; ASTRA's body knocked offline; survivors flee.
  • Recover downed member + crystal; head back. Level 2.

Characters present

All except Gerthorlemue (still in his pod; 0 mentions).

  • ASTRA — scanned for the camp, negotiated, plugged into the power grid (→84%); body knocked offline in the fight, reverting to the ship matrix. Deadpan dark comedy.
  • Ronon Dex — recruited guide; carried the heavy crystal; raged and killed multiple hobgoblins (incl. a crit); made the survivors flee.
  • Gobby — led with sharp sight; brewed the tequila; got the goblins drunk; crowned "king."
  • G.L.I.M.M. — shifted forms (blob/turtle/monkey), morphed sickle-arms, digested a crystal, made a detached "clone," set off the explosion, cast Faerie Fire — then dropped ("dead").
  • Kael Voss — cautious/moral voice; wanted a hobgoblin captive via persuasion; ex-Vanguard reveal.
  • Baldy ("Big D") — the mining muscle (huge carry capacity); pulled the biggest crystals; mostly out of the final fight.

NPCs

  • Ronon Dex — NPC stranger → recruited ally.
  • Goblins & hobgoblins (mining-camp guards) — dim, easily manipulated; initially passive, turned hostile after the camp burned. Drunk ones killed by the explosion; 5 sober ones fought and lost/fled.
  • The goblin "king" — a hobgoblin in a cheap paper crown; deposed by Gobby.
  • Captain Talvos — not mentioned this session.

Locations

  • The asteroid — barren; both the crew's and Ronon's ships crashed here. (DM mused it was meant to be a prison but "mildly forgot that bit.")
  • The crew's crashed ship (Silver Gull) — powered down; rations, wiring, spirits. Still dark at session end.
  • Ronon's crashed ship — burned-out hull, nothing of value.
  • The mining encampment (~2 km port) — abandoned/lightly-staffed ferrocrystal camp with a main hall/throne room, food-printer, company logs, and an accessible power grid. Destroyed by fire.

Combat

One real fight, at the camp exit: crew (Ronon, G.L.I.M.M., ASTRA's body) vs. 5 enemies (3 hobgoblins, 2 goblins), after failed deception + persuasion. G.L.I.M.M. cast Faerie Fire and killed several with sickles before being dropped to 0; Ronon raged, crit, and finished several; ASTRA's body was struck and dissipated offline. Crew win; survivors flee. Plus the tequila+torch explosion (~8d6 fireball) that wiped out the drunk goblins beforehand.

Loot / resources

  • Ceruleum ferrocrystal — ~100+ kg (objective complete + spares). Fuel/repair feedstock.
  • Gobby's spirits — ~10–12 bottles, weaponized as tequila.
  • Camp logs — intel on the previous mining company (little on the galaxy itself).
  • A broken alien console/scrap — unreadable (foreign tech).
  • Ronon's kit joins the party (2 daggers, leather armor, revolver + ~10 bullets, torch, etc.).
  • A drunk hobgoblin captive carried out; a joke lawnmower; the goblin throne (crumbled).

Objective status after S1

  • ✅ Ferrocrystal retrieved. ✅ ASTRA charged (84%). ❌ Ship not yet re-powered. ❌ Talvos: no progress.

Threads left open

  • How to actually use the ferrocrystal to re-power/repair the ship.
  • Where they are; whether home is reachable.
  • ASTRA's downed body + G.L.I.M.M. "dead" — both need the ship restored / reviving.
  • Fleeing hobgoblins could return; a captive + burning camp left behind.
  • Ronon's unexplained grudge "against the people of this galaxy."
  • The dropped "prison" premise.

Memorable moments

  • Gobby's identity crisis: "I am a turtle… but I am a man. What is a turtle?"
  • G.L.I.M.M. claiming to be "older than anything and everything" — then admitting he's a lab experiment.
  • Kael's intro: "I don't like bad guys. I'm totally normal."
  • Gobby crowned: "I am the king… the fun water bringer."
  • ASTRA, after draining the grid and torching the camp, gives the survivors "zero time," framed as "lessening their suffering."
  • The signature set-piece: flood the hall with tequila, then torch it on the way out.

partyLog.title: Repel Boarders, Power the Ship
beats: Back at the dark Gull, we plugged ASTRA's body into a console — the ship powered on and ASTRA revived, listing dead systems (internal sensors, engines, most weaponry).
Goblins had snuck aboard, kicking off a long, comedic room-by-room boarding fight.
Standout kills: Gobby fist-killed the drunk hobgoblin he'd carried 2 km; G.L.I.M.M. decapitated several; Ronon's 'thumb-war' made a goblin kill itself; Kael self-healed while mobbed.
Cleared and looted, we deployed ferrocrystal-eating repair drones, re-attached the front door, salvaged ship weapons, and leveled to 3.
partyLog.full:
Summary

Session 2 opens with a long DM recap of Session 1, then picks up with the crew back aboard the still- dark, grounded Silver Gull, carrying ASTRA's downed body (and Baldy still carrying a drunk hobgoblin). They plug ASTRA's body into a ship console — which powers the ship back up, flickers the lights on, and revives ASTRA. She reports many systems still down (internal sensors, engines, most weaponry) and urges immediate repairs, starting with the missing front door.

Before repairs can begin, they discover goblins and hobgoblins have snuck aboard, hiding in the bedrooms and a lower engineering level. This kicks off the session's single, very long boarding fight — a chaotic, comedic room-by-room clear through corridors, cockpit, bedrooms, and a bathroom. Gobby fist-kills the drunk hobgoblin he carried 2 km; G.L.I.M.M. morphs a glaive/sickles and decapitates several goblins; a gunslinger lines two goblins up and kills both with one shot; Ronon Dex runs absurd "thumb war" gambits (one goblin literally kills itself). Kael is mobbed to low HP and self-heals with Channel Divinity.

After clearing all enemies (including a couple of tougher hobgoblins), the crew loot the bodies, deploy ferrocrystal-eating repair drones, re-attach the front door, and claim salvaged ship weapons. Everyone takes a long rest and levels up to 3. The ship is now actively self-repairing — the session ends on that beat.

Key beats

  • Long DM recap of Session 1.
  • Crew return to the dark, grounded Gull with ASTRA's body.
  • ASTRA plugged into a console → ship powers on, lights up, ASTRA revives.
  • ASTRA lists systems still down (internal sensors, engines, most weaponry); urges repairs + the door.
  • Gobby fist-kills the carried drunk hobgoblin.
  • Discovery of goblin/hobgoblin boarders; initiative → long room-by-room fight.
  • Comedic kills: Ronon's thumb-war (a goblin kills itself), G.L.I.M.M.'s decapitations, a lined-up double-kill shot, Gobby drinking mid-fight.
  • All boarders killed; bodies looted.
  • Repair drones deployed (consume ferrocrystal); front door re-attached; ship weapons salvaged.
  • Long rest; level up to 3. Ship self-repairing.

Characters present

  • ASTRA — revived at the console; powered the ship on; acted as exposition/quest-giver; limited in combat; repeatedly nagged the crew to repair the internal weapons system.
  • Ronon Dex — feral comedy: repeated "thumb war"/axe-endurance gambits (a goblin killed itself); held the door for re-attachment (rolled terribly on Investigating it); showered aboard; grabbed a salvaged pistol + hunting rifle for future proficiency.
  • Gobby — punched/killed the drunk hobgoblin; fought bare-handed while drinking beer from his shell. (Newer player being taught the rules.)
  • G.L.I.M.M. — glaive then dual sickles; decapitated multiple goblins; big melee damage (a max-damage hit).
  • Baldy — present but passive (relaxing in a chair); associated with gunplay + repairs.
  • Kael Voss — cast Bless; used Channel Divinity to self-heal while mobbed at low HP.
  • Gerthorlemue — not active; presumably still in the stasis pod.

NPCs

  • Boarding goblins & hobgoblins — hostile; snuck aboard, appearing from bedrooms + a lower level; includes a couple of tougher/"fancy" hobgoblins. No named boss this session. One goblin killed itself during Ronon's thumb-war.
  • The drunk hobgoblin — carried from S1; killed early by Gobby.
  • Captain Talvos — referenced only ("alive, dead, or somewhere considerably stranger"); still lost.
  • "10 crew members aboard nobody has fully encountered" — mentioned in the recap; never developed.

Locations

  • SSV Silver Gull interior — the session's main setting. Multi-level: cockpit, corridors, crew bedrooms, a bathroom, an engineering level with a ladder down, and a console/charging station. Initially dark; front door missing (from S1) then reattached. Also: a handprint scanner (Baldy's print recognized), a shower, weapon storage, and a teased unactivated ship "feature."
  • The asteroid / unknown system — the Gull remains grounded near the rift.
  • (Referenced) the destroyed mining camp, 2 km west.

Combat

Single major encounter: repelling the boarding party — a long multi-turn, room-by-room fight (the bulk of the session). Numerous goblins + several hobgoblins (incl. two "stronger" ones), which kept appearing from bedrooms/the lower level. Kael was mobbed to low HP and self-healed; Ronon dropped to ~12 HP and used Second Wind. No PC deaths; total party victory. (0 XP auto-assigned — the table doesn't use XP.)

Loot / resources

  • Ferrocrystal — the S1 haul now feeds the repair drones (they "eat" it to repair the ship).
  • Goblin weapon loot — ~2 longswords, ~7 short swords, ~7 short bows (Kael plans to study weapons on a rest).
  • Salvaged ship weapons — pistols and "hunting rifles"/"space guns"; Ronon claims a pistol + rifle.
  • Progression — all PCs to level 3.

Objective status after S2

  • ✅ Ferrocrystal (secured, now in use). ✅ ASTRA charge (used to re-power the ship). 🔄 Ship repairs in progress (door done; drones running; internal sensors/engines/weaponry still down). ❌ Talvos: no progress.

Threads left open

  • Talvos's fate; getting off the asteroid (engines still down).
  • The teased unactivated ship "feature."
  • The "10 unencountered crew members."
  • Where the boarders came from (players suspected someone "spawning" them).
  • The unknown star system / the rift.

Memorable moments

  • DM recap: "The first thing that happened was Gobby ripped the front door off. That's one. These things happen."
  • ASTRA on the S1 explosion: she'd have given the goblins "a year on this rock anyway. Then she looked at the fire and revised that figure to zero."
  • Ronon's thumb-war: a goblin cuts off its own thumb, then smashes its own finger with a hammer and dies — "I might not have done any damage… but I made him kill himself." Later: "Why am I shooting them when I can just tell them to kill himself?"
  • The lined-up double kill: "Bang! Straight through one goblin's head, and then the other."
  • Ronon's self-deprecation: "I couldn't kill a goblin to save my life… but I can have a shower."
  • Meta note: Ronon Dex is intentionally the Stargate Atlantis character — "Jason Momoa before he was Jason Momoa popular."

partyLog.title: Sandra's Folly
beats: Airborne, ASTRA ran the first real scan (Keth Minor, Vorrn-7, a [CORRUPTED] ring) and we chose the nearest contact — the adrift derelict Sandra's Folly, aft sheared clean off.
Gobby and Baldy stayed on the Gull; the rest looted 6 vacc-suit patches and an unknown sidearm, and found a green-glowing stasis pod with a figure inside.
In the cargo hold we hit The Hollow, a sensor-invisible rift creature. Ronon recognized it; it shrugged off our attacks and drifted out through the aft wound (downing Kael, nat 1).
ASTRA revived Kael, G.L.I.M.M. reformed from a puddle, and we recovered 2 hyperfold fuel cells. The pod stayed sealed.
partyLog.full:
Summary

With the three-day repair skip behind them and the Silver Gull back under power (and airborne), ASTRA presented the crew with the first real sensor scan of the system. Three destinations sat within fuel range; the crew chose the closest contact: "Unidentified Vessel — Adrift," a mid-size freighter, dark, no transponder, one faint life sign, drifting toward the edge of range. ASTRA read the partial hull markings and estimated the ship's name as Sandra's Folly — a hauler roughly 40% larger than the Silver Gull, its entire aft section sheared clean off as if something had cut through it without slowing.

Gobby and Baldy stayed behind to watch the Silver Gull (Gobby was, as ever, extremely drunk). The rest docked at a blown-out starboard airlock and entered. Thin but breathable air; partial artificial gravity running off a dying emergency micro-cell. Fanning out (loudly), the crew found 6 vacc-suit hull patches and an unknown-make sidearm (a worn, non-UGC compact pistol, loaded + one spare mag), and located the Medical Bay — where a single stasis pod glowed faint green in the dark, a figure inside, blood on the floor near the door.

Before anyone reached the pod, they found The Hollow in the cargo hold — a rift creature, invisible to every sensor, three metres tall when it chose a shape. Ronon Dex recognised it instantly — these are what dismantled his civilisation — and told them: don't fire kinetic, don't melee, leave now. They didn't. A brutal, one-sided fight followed; the Hollow was immune to psychic, resistant to nonmagical piercing, and deflected most kinetic attacks (force and slashing worked). It never died — on Round 3 its "departure condition" was met and it simply drifted out through the aft shear wound into space, dealing 7 damage to everyone in its path (Kael rolled a nat 1, took 14, and went down). The crew ended battered but alive; ASTRA revived Kael with Cure Wounds, Glimm reformed from a puddle, Ronon stood at 5 HP. Searching the hold afterward turned up 2 Hyperfold Fuel Cells (jump-drive fuel — flagged important). The session ended with the pod survivor still sealed and much of Sandra's Folly unexplored.

Key beats

  • Three-day repair skip; Silver Gull re-powered and airborne. ASTRA shares the first system scan.
  • Crew pick the adrift derelict (≈ Sandra's Folly) over the two other leads.
  • Dock at a blown starboard airlock; Gobby + Baldy stay on the Gull.
  • Loot sweep: 6 vacc-suit patches, 1 unknown sidearm (Kael).
  • Find the Medical Bay: an occupied, green-glowing stasis pod (blood on the floor).
  • Discover The Hollow in the cargo hold; Ronon recognises it and warns them off.
  • Combat — the Hollow deflects/absorbs most attacks; Glimm phases through it taking backlash, drops to 2 HP; Kael Hexes it (Int) and Shields Ronon.
  • Round 3: the Hollow leaves through the aft shear wound; AoE on exit downs Kael (nat 1 → 14).
  • Post-combat: ASTRA Cure Wounds revives Kael; Glimm reforms; find 2 Hyperfold Fuel Cells.
  • Pod survivor left sealed; rest of the ship unexplored → carries into Session 4.

Characters present

  • ASTRA — ran the scan; identified Sandra's Folly; in combat held a crewmate clear of the Hollow; post-fight Cure Wounds (2nd) on Kael.
  • Kael Voss ("evil mode") — Hex (Int at disadvantage) + Eldritch Blast (missed); Shield of Faith on Ronon; downed by the Hollow's exit AoE (nat 1, 14 dmg), stabilised/revived.
  • G.L.I.M.M. — dual sickle-arms + Action Surge (3 attacks); phased through the Hollow twice taking 18 + 5 backlash; ended at 2 HP and collapsed into a puddle (reformed after).
  • Ronon Dex — opened with his pistol (missed); rage + damage resistance soaked a 32-damage hit down to 4; recognised the Hollow; ended at 5 HP.
  • Gobby & Baldy — stayed aboard the Silver Gull.
  • Gerthorlemue — the figure in the stasis pod (unopened this session; woken in S4).

NPCs / creatures

  • The Hollow — a rift creature aboard Sandra's Folly's cargo hold. Sensor-invisible, gravity-warping, immune to psychic, resistant to nonmagical physical, deflects kinetic fire. Did not die — it left when its interest expired. Full stat block & lore → `../../bestiary/the-hollow.md`. Ronon: it left because they weren't worth its time — that is not the same as being safe. It knows what they smell like now.
  • The stasis-pod survivor = Gerthorlemue (revealed S4).
  • Captain Talvos — no sign; still lost.

Locations

  • Sandra's Folly — a mid-size hauling freighter (~40% larger than the Gull), dark, no transponder, aft sheared clean off by something precise and fast. Breathable thin air, failing micro-cell gravity, scorch/impact scoring. Explored: starboard airlocks, a storage room, crew quarters, the port-side medical bay, the cargo hold. Much remains unexplored.
  • The system (per the nav scan): the Gull's position ringed by the Keth Minor Cluster, the Vorrn-7 System, and a [CORRUPTED] ring structure (see below), plus rift-radiation blackout zones and an asteroid field.

Loot / resources (confirmed this session)

  • 1× Unknown-make sidearm — compact non-UGC pistol, worn grip, loaded + 1 spare mag (Kael).
  • 2× Hyperfold Fuel Cells — Silver Gull jump-drive fuel (a 3rd is found in S4). Flagged as important to track. See `../inventory.md`.

HP going into Session 4

Kael — down/stabilised/revived, low • Glimm — 2 HP, reformed from puddle • Ronon — 5 HP, still raging.

Threads left open

  • The rest of Sandra's Folly (unsearched rooms, more loot).
  • The [CORRUPTED] ring structure — described here as the corrupted ship visible in the rift, its writing in an ancient language possibly older than ASTRA herself. See `../../lore/ancients-and-tech.md`.

Memorable

  • Ronon's warning and, after: these are the creatures that wiped out my entire civilisation — a small one.

partyLog.full:
Summary

Session 4 opened with the crew cracking the stasis pod in Sandra's Folly's medical bay — revealing Gerthorlemue, a 4,000-year-old High Elf entertainer/wizard from Blackshire, Earth, stranded in emergency stasis since a cactus-related stage mishap. He took the situation (missing ship aft, rift creature, and the news that the UGC doesn't exist in this galaxy) reasonably well, and joined the crew. He mentioned that something vast inside the rift had noticed him during transit and left a mark on his forehead — the DM's (classified) "Magician's Eye."

The crew stripped Sandra's Folly (final haul incl. a 3rd Hyperfold Fuel Cell, 2 boarding cutlasses, 3 frag grenades, and more), returned to the Silver Gull with fuel to spare, and set course for Vorrn-7 — a gas giant with a faint life reading on a moon and a signal ASTRA couldn't identify. En route they were ambushed by an Apostles of the Threshold vessel, triggering the Silver Gull's first ship-to-ship combat. The crew manned stations and, over several rounds, crippled the Apostle ship's engines (Ronon's Heavy Autocannon dealing a near-crit 50), swung to its unshielded rear, and — realising the small ship could be captured intact — rammed it and fired Ronon through a breach (packed with six of Gobby's bottles and a breach mine) into the enemy.

Inside, Ronon shoved a gunner into space (nat 20 athletics) and battered the captain; Kael's intimidation flopped (nat 1) but he chopped the captain to 3 HP. The captain — serene, out of weapons — screamed "All hail the gods and the craters!" and hit self-destruct: a 12-second / two-round countdown. The twist: Apostle self-destructs are three physical blue modules on the hull, unstoppable by any terminal — destroy all three or the ship blows. In a frantic two rounds the crew got two modules (including Baldy's legendary shot through the Silver Gull's own windscreen, a total of 22), but Gerthorlemue's 4,000-year-old gun misfired one short and the third module survived. The Apostles overcharged their shields backward to reflect the blast straight at the Silver Gull. The ship (150 HP, shields up) took half — but Glimm, still floating in open space, took 27; instant death was 28. He made his death save (clean die), and ASTRA — who'd forgotten all session she was a healer — finally cast Cure Wounds and brought him back. Everyone survived; the Apostle ship was gone; the crew are now firmly on the Apostles' bad side.

Key beats

  • Crack the stasis pod → Gerthorlemue revealed and recruited; he mentions the rift-mark ("Magician's Eye", DM-classified).
  • Final loot sweep of Sandra's Folly; return to the Gull with ample fuel (3 hyperfold cells).
  • Ronon briefs the galaxy's three factions (Iron Directorate, Apostles, Sovereign Horizon) and confirms rift creatures killed his people — and one faction worships them.
  • Set course for Vorrn-7.
  • Ship combat vs. an Apostles vessel (perception 16 to ID it). Crew take stations.
  • R1: Kael Aggressive Positioning; Ronon's Heavy Autocannon lands a near-crit 50; enemy engines crippled/locked.
  • R2: swing to the unshielded rear; Kael grants Ronon a 2nd action → two autocannon hits; Glimm heals ship HP each round.
  • R3: realise the ship is tiny and capturable → ram + fire Ronon through a breach to board.
  • Boarding: Ronon shoves a gunner into space (nat 20); Glimm blinds another with a plasmoid blob; Kael chops the captain to 3 HP (intimidation nat 1).
  • Captain triggers self-destruct (3 physical blue modules, terminal-proof).
  • Crew destroy 2 of 3 modules (Baldy's through-the-windscreen 22; Gobby's flak turret 21); Gerthorlemue's ancient gun misfires one short (16 vs DC 17).
  • Ship detonates; Apostles reflect the blast off overcharged rear shields back at the Gull.
  • Gull (150 HP) takes half; Glimm in open space takes 27 (28 = instant death), makes his death save; ASTRA remembers Cure Wounds and revives him.
  • All survive. No loot (ship destroyed). Crew now in bad standing with the Apostles.

Characters present (with confirmed player↔character mapping)

Ship-combat stations for the Apostle fight:

StationPlayerCharacter
PilotJustin(unconfirmed — see roster note)
Captain—Kael Voss
Port GunnerDerekRonon Dex
Starboard GunnerZionBaldy
EngineerZachG.L.I.M.M.
Science OfficerJayden(unconfirmed)
ShieldsStevenGobby

Plus ASTRA (Isaac) on the bridge, and Gerthorlemue newly aboard (manned a gun station for the final module shot). (This table is the source of the confirmed mapping — see `../../characters/README.md`.)

Highlights: Ronon — autocannon near-crit 50, boarding leap, gunner-into-space nat 20, self-heal via Warrior of the Gods. Baldy — the impossible captain-swap pistol shot through the Gull's own viewport (22). Gobby — cold-shot the enemy engines; flak-turret module kill (21). Kael — positioning calls; chopped the captain to 3. G.L.I.M.M. — engineer power-reroutes + ship heals; blinded a gunner; nearly died in the blast. ASTRA — Bless on the shooters, then the clutch Cure Wounds. Gerthorlemue — first outing; his ancient gun misfired at the worst moment.

NPCs

  • The Apostle captain — fanatical, unafraid ("I am going to die with you… The craters will save me"); 58 HP; triggered the self-destruct. NOT Captain Talvos.
  • Apostle crew — a gunner shoved into space; another blinded. All lost with the ship.
  • Captain Talvos — still missing; no appearance.

Locations

  • Sandra's Folly (medical bay + rest of ship) — finally stripped; Gerthorlemue recovered.
  • En route to Vorrn-7 — open space; site of the ship battle.
  • The Apostle vessel — a deceptively tiny ship (barely more than a cockpit); boarded, then self-destructed.

Loot / resources

  • From Sandra's Folly (final): 3× Hyperfold Fuel Cells (confirmed total, locked storage near the engine room), 2× Boarding Cutlasses, 3× Fragmentation Grenades, 6× vacc-suit patches, emergency rations + medical supplies, plus the earlier unknown sidearm. Fuel is now ample — the map's old max-travel-radius can be ignored.
  • From the Apostle ship: nothing (it destroyed itself).
  • See the running tracker → `../inventory.md`.

Ship & standing status

  • Silver Gull: 150 HP; took 27 blast damage (half, shields up) — healthy overall. Front windscreen now has a bullet hole (Baldy's shot).
  • Factions: now in bad standing with the Apostles of the Threshold. See `../../lore/factions.md`.

Threads left open

  • What the Magician's Eye actually is/does (DM-classified).
  • Vorrn-7 — the gas-giant moon signal they're still headed for.
  • Captain Talvos — still out there.
  • Standing with all three factions — off to a rough start with the Apostles; the Hollow still at large.

Lessons the crew wrote down

  • "Next time — shoot the blue things first." Apostle ships have a three-point self-destruct that no terminal can stop once triggered; the blue hull markers are the targets.
  • Apostle shields can be directionally overcharged to weaponise their own explosion.
  • The DM's reminder: death is permanent. Glimm survived by a single point.

whoswho.name: ASTRA
whoswho.text: Our ship's mind, walking in a mobile chassis after the rift broke her old restraints. Deadpan, precise, darkly funny; our sensor suite, information hub, and (eventually remembered) field medic. Admits her knowledge has gaps since the crash.

whoswho.name: Kael Voss
whoswho.text: Exiled conquest-paladin from Wild Space; his holy strikes flicker with dark eldritch power. Casts Bless, Hex, Eldritch Blast, Shield of Faith; can 'read' Ancient ruins. 'I don't like bad guys. I'm totally normal.'

whoswho.name: Baldy ('Big D')
whoswho.text: Four-armed bugbear Deadeye gunslinger and card-shark. The mining muscle (~420 lb carry), a recognized ship scanner-print, and the crew's impossible-shot artist.

whoswho.name: Gobby
whoswho.text: Tortle Drunken Master monk and wandering brewmaster whose martial arts run on whatever cosmic booze he last drank. Can neutralize toxins into temporary powers and smell what's inside a sealed door. Crowned 'king' of a goblin camp.

whoswho.name: G.L.I.M.M.
whoswho.text: Resurrected Plasmoid clone whose body reshapes into any weapon and reforms from a puddle after lethal hits. Near-immune to poison and acid; our melee workhorse. Came one point from permanent death against the Apostles.

whoswho.name: Ronon Dex
whoswho.text: Last survivor of the extinct Satedan Dominion, from another galaxy; a lethal Barbarian/Gunslinger and our local guide. Recognizes rift creatures on sight. Carries an unexplained grudge 'against the people of this galaxy.'

whoswho.name: Gerthorlemue
whoswho.text: Newly-woken high-elf busker/Abjurer, ~4,000 years lost in stasis aboard Sandra's Folly. Warm, theatrical, grieving his dead troupe; carries the mysterious Magician's Eye that opens near Ancient tech. Still thinks it's practically SY 2551.

whoswho.name: Captain Elias Renn Talvos
whoswho.text: Our legendary commanding officer, 'a legend in everything except personality.' Suited up for a live-hull walk during the rift and was pulled into the OTHER flow (Flow Beta). Finding any trace of him is the campaign's long arc.

leads: Find Captain Talvos — pulled into Flow Beta, a different flow than the ship, so wherever he landed isn't necessarily where we crashed.
Reach Vorrn-7 — our current forward objective: a ringed ice/gas giant with a faint life reading and a signal ASTRA couldn't identify.
The three scanned destinations — Keth Minor Cluster (oxygen-rich, unnatural structures, biosignatures), Vorrn-7, and the [CORRUPTED] ring (a possible Ancient Gate, writing older than ASTRA).
Why do we instinctively know the scanned planets' names? (flagged in Session 3)
The Magician's Eye — Gerthorlemue's rift-mark; it will announce us the moment we enter an Ancient ruin.
The Apostles of the Threshold — now in bad standing. They won't parley, carry a three-point (blue-module) self-destruct, and reflect their own detonation. 'Next time — shoot the blue things first.'
The Hollow is still out there — a rift creature we couldn't kill, and it 'knows what we smell like.'
Ronon's grudge against 'the people of this galaxy,' still unexplained.
The rest of Sandra's Folly — some rooms went unsearched.
Restore the Silver Gull fully — internal sensors, engines, internal weaponry, all 6 turret hardpoints, and shields still need work. A hidden ship 'feature' was teased in S2 and never found.
The dropped 'prison' premise — the DM framed the asteroid as a prison early and may bring it back.
Fleeing hobgoblin survivors from the burned mining camp could return.
Getting home / figuring out where 'here' is — outside the Luminara Galaxy; whether home is reachable is unknown.
The Iron Directorate and Sovereign Horizon — the galaxy's other two superpowers, both currently Neutral / no contact.

locations.name: The Shattered Expanse
locations.info: The crew's known region — the lawless frontier sector where the rift stranded the Silver Gull. Click again to open the sector chart.

locations.name: The Coil (jump gate)
locations.info: The living Ancient hyper-gate at the heart of the Expanse — a weathered alien ring, still fully functional after untold ages. Ships travel sector-to-sector through it; nobody built it, nobody can shut it off. A possible road home.

locations.name: Halberd's Rest
locations.info: The sector's great neutral-ground free port, built inside the gutted hull of a derelict Directorate dreadnought near The Coil. Every faction, pirate crew and trader passes through; weapons are peace-bonded at the door. The closest thing the Expanse has to a capital.

locations.name: Sundowner
locations.info: A rogue, star-less planet turned into one endless casino-city, lit against the dark. Debts, information and ships change hands over the tables. Baldy has almost certainly been banned from somewhere here.

locations.name: Gallows Reach
locations.info: Seat of the sector's most powerful pirate lords — a bounty-and-black-market hub where crews are hired, prizes fenced, and reputations made or ended.

locations.name: Cindermoor
locations.info: A volcanic refinery world; cartels refine hyper-dense thermite and reactor fuel from the magma flats. Choking, wealthy, dangerous — a source of turret-grade materials.

locations.name: Ossuary Fields
locations.info: The Ember Drift's ship-graveyard system, anchored by Ossuary — centuries of wrecks dragged down its gravity well, now a sprawling salvage operation.

locations.name: Ossuary
locations.info: A ship-graveyard world: centuries of wrecks dragged down its gravity well, now a sprawling salvage settlement. Ferrocrystal, hyperfold cells and stranger things turn up here.

locations.name: Tarn
locations.info: A frozen cryo-mining world; cheap labor, colder politics. Ice hauled out, questions not asked.

locations.name: Marrow
locations.info: A cracked desert world where water is the black-market currency; hideouts and dust — perfect for disappearing.

locations.name: Greenhollow (system)
locations.info: The Verdant Fringe's star system — jungle worlds veined with Verdite, contested by rival prospector gangs. For Ronon Dex, the first place in this galaxy that could get his people's tech running again.

locations.name: Greenhollow
locations.info: A lush jungle world veined with Verdite — the fuel for Satedan Aether-Core drives. For Ronon Dex, the first place that could revive his people's tech. Heavily contested by prospector gangs.

locations.name: Sib Vael
locations.info: A warm ocean world of smuggler coves and floating markets, famous for exotic brews distilled from bioluminescent kelp and reef-spirits. Gobby would sell an arm to dock here.

locations.name: Bexley's Landing
locations.info: A human-founded frontier town-world — the most 'ordinary' place in the sector: farms, a spaceport bar, and a sheriff who means well and is badly outgunned.

locations.name: Choir Rim
locations.info: The Cold Rim's star system, anchored by The Choir — a spire-covered shrine world where the Apostles of the Threshold keep a mission, preaching the rifts and quietly recruiting.

locations.name: The Choir
locations.info: A spire-covered shrine world on the rim where the Apostles of the Threshold keep a mission — preaching the rifts and quietly recruiting. A foothold of the faithful, not a garrison. (The crew are already on the Apostles' bad side.)

locations.name: Ferrum Hold
locations.info: A rim mining holding leaning toward the Iron Directorate, buying ore and loyalty in equal measure. Orderly, watchful, unwelcoming to outlaws — but not a garrison.

locations.name: Vorrn (system)
locations.info: The crew's current corner of the Expanse — the system that holds Vorrn-7 and Keth Minor, and where the crew acquire the full sector chart.

locations.name: Vorrn-7
locations.info: A ringed ice/gas giant and a moon with a faint life reading and a signal ASTRA couldn't identify. The crew's current forward destination.

locations.name: Keth Minor
